title: Game of Thrones
wiki_lead:
Game of Thrones is an American fantasy drama television series created by David Benioff and D. B. Weiss for HBO. It is the first adaptation of A Song of Ice and Fire, a series of high fantasy novels by George R. R. Martin, and the first in what would become the Game of Thrones franchise. The show premiered on HBO in the United States on April 17, 2011, and concluded on May 19, 2019, with 73 episodes broadcast over eight seasons.
Set on the fictional continents of Westeros and Essos, Game of Thrones has a large ensemble cast and follows several story arcs throughout the course of the show. The first major arc concerns the Iron Throne of the Seven Kingdoms of Westeros through a web of political conflicts among the noble families, either vying to claim the throne or fighting for independence. The second major arc focuses on the last descendant of the realm's deposed ruling dynasty, who has been exiled to Essos and is plotting to return and reclaim the throne. The third follows the Night's Watch, a military order defending the realm against threats from beyond the Seven Kingdoms' northern border.
Game of Thrones attracted a record viewership on HBO and has a broad, active, and international fan base. Many critics and publications have named the show one of the greatest television series of all time. Critics have praised the series for its acting, complex characters, story, scope, and production values, although its frequent use of nudity and violence (including sexual violence) generated controversy. The final season received significant criticism for its reduced length and creative decisions, with many considering it a disappointing conclusion. The series received 59 Primetime Emmy Awards, the most by a drama series, including Outstanding Drama Series in 2015, 2016, 2018 and 2019. Its other awards and nominations include three Hugo Awards for Best Dramatic Presentation, a Peabody Award, and five nominations for the Golden Globe Award for Best Television Series – Drama.

Two prequel series, House of the Dragon and A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, premiered on HBO in 2022 and 2026, respectively.

Premise

Game of Thrones is roughly based on the storylines of the A Song of Ice and Fire book series by George R. R. Martin, set in the fictional Seven Kingdoms of Westeros and the continent of Essos. The series follows several simultaneous plotlines. The first story arc follows a war of succession among competing claimants for control of the Iron Throne of the Seven Kingdoms, with other noble families fighting for independence from the throne. The second concerns the actions of the exiled scion to reclaim the throne; the third chronicles the threat of the impending winter, as well as the legendary creatures and fierce peoples of the North.

Weiss for HBO, adapting the epic novel series A Song of Ice and Fire by George R. R. Martin. The series, which premiered on April 17, 2011, and concluded on May 19, 2019, spans eight seasons and 73 episodes, totaling approximately 70 hours and 14 minutes (early seasons averaging around 55 minutes per episode, later seasons up to 82 minutes), chronicling brutal power struggles among noble houses vying for control of the Iron Throne in the fictional continent of Westeros, amid looming supernatural threats from the North and East. Set against a backdrop of medieval-inspired realism, political intrigue, graphic violence, and moral ambiguity, it features complex characters whose alliances and betrayals drive the narrative, diverging from traditional fantasy tropes by emphasizing human frailty and unpredictable outcomes over heroic inevitability. The production's scale, with budgets exceeding $10 million per episode in later seasons, enabled expansive location shooting in Northern Ireland, Croatia, Iceland, and Malta, contributing to its immersive world-building and visual spectacle. Game of Thrones achieved unprecedented acclaim, securing 59 Primetime Emmy Awards, including a record 12 wins for its final season, and dominating viewership charts with episodes routinely surpassing 10 million U.S. viewers on premiere nights, amplified by global streaming and piracy metrics that underscored its cultural penetration. Its influence extended to merchandise sales, tourism boosts at filming sites like Dubrovnik's walls representing King's Landing, and linguistic integrations such as "red wedding" entering common parlance for shocking betrayals. Notable controversies arose from deviations from Martin's unfinished novels after Season 5, culminating in widespread backlash against the abbreviated eighth season for perceived rushed pacing, inconsistent character arcsâparticularly Daenerys Targaryen's descent into tyrannyâand unsatisfying resolutions that alienated portions of its audience, as evidenced by review-bombing on platforms and petitions for rewrites. Showrunners Benioff and Weiss defended the choices as intentional subversions rooted in the story's themes of cyclical power and human imperfection, though Martin has noted the adaptation's independence from his yet-to-be-completed book vision. Despite the finale's divisiveness, the series' legacy endures through spin-offs like House of the Dragon and its role in elevating prestige cable drama's global dominance.
